title: mappingAS: Spatial Range Metrics, MapBiomas Habitat Conversion and Fire, and Protected-Area Overlap for IUCN Criterion B Screening
description:
mappingAS (Mapping Area of Species) is an R package, with an accompanying Shiny application, for preliminary species extinction-risk screening under Criterion B of the IUCN Red List. Starting from a set of occurrence points, it estimates each species' geographic range and quantifies the pressures acting on it using Brazil's national datasets, in a workflow familiar to users of GeoCAT.

For every species it computes:

  • Range metrics - the Extent of Occurrence (EOO, minimum convex polygon) and the Area of Occupancy (AOO, 2 km grid) on a data-centred equal-area projection, with provisional Criterion B size categories (screening only).
  • Habitat conversion - the percentage of converted (anthropic) versus remaining natural land cover within the EOO and AOO from MapBiomas, with a full per-class breakdown and land-cover time series (1985-2024).
  • Fire - the share of the range burned at least once and burned-area time series, from MapBiomas Fire.
  • Protected-area overlap - the overlap of occurrences, EOO and AOO with Brazilian federal Conservation Units (ICMBio / INDE), including the habitat that is both natural and protected.

MapBiomas data are read locally over the network via GDAL '/vsicurl/' (no Google Earth Engine account required) or server-side through Google Earth Engine for large-scale assessments. Outputs include interactive Leaflet maps, publication-ready static maps, interactive charts, spatial (shapefile / GeoPackage) and raster (GeoTIFF) exports, and a written, referenced assessment report (HTML, plain text or Word). The bundled Shiny application ties the whole workflow together, with no code required.

Note. The categories produced are provisional and intended for screening only; they do not replace a formal IUCN Red List assessment, which also requires the sub-conditions of fragmentation or few locations, continuing decline and extreme fluctuation.

Source code and documentation: https://github.com/lucasbarreirageo/mappingAS
